layers.source_title: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Wetland Classification Codes
layers.description: This table provides a crosswalk from U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, National Wetlands Inventory (NWI) wetlands data, as defined by the Federal Wetland Mapping Standard, to the complete wetland definitions, as defined by the Federal Wetlands Classification Standard. The table should be joined with the NWI wetlands data using the 'Attribute' field. This will provide users with a full wetland or deepwater habitat description for each polygon.
layers.summary: NWI_Code_Definitions_Table — Cowardin Wetland Classification definitions for corresponding NWI Map Codes. This table provides a crosswalk from the National Wetlands Inventory wetlands data, as defined by the Federal Wetland Mapping Standard, to the complete wetland definitions, as defined by the Federal Wetlands Classification Standard.
layers.citation: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, National Standards and Support Team, October 2024.

columns.name: attribute
columns.description: Alphanumeric code identifying the wetland or deepwater classification of the polygon.

columns.name: system
columns.description: Alpha code identifying the system

columns.name: system_name
columns.description: Name assigned to a complex of wetlands and deepwater habitats that share the influence of similar hydrologic, geomorphologic, chemical or biological factors.

columns.name: system_definition
columns.description: Definition of the System  - a complex of wetlands and deepwater habitats that share the influence of similar hydrologic, geomorphologic, chemical or biological factors.

columns.name: subsystem
columns.description: Numeric code identifying the subsystem

columns.name: subsystem_name
columns.description: Name assigned to subdivide System designations into more specific categories.

columns.name: subsystem_definition
columns.description: Definitions in terms of water permanence, gradient, substrate, and the extent of floodplain development, or tidal influence.

columns.name: class
columns.description: Alpha code identifying the class

columns.name: class_name
columns.description: The highest taxonomic unit below the Subsystem level, usually describing either the dominant life form of the vegetation or the physiography and composition of the substrate.

columns.name: class_definition
columns.description: Describes the general appearance of the habitat in terms of either the dominant life form of the vegetation, or the physiography and composition of the substrate.

columns.name: subclass
columns.description: Numeric code identifying the subclass

columns.name: subclass_name
columns.description: Name assigned to further define life forms or substrate type.

columns.name: subclass_definition
columns.description: Definition assigned to define the specific life form, or substrate with the greatest areal coverage present.

columns.name: split_class
columns.description: Alpha code identifying the split class

columns.name: split_class_name
columns.description: Name assigned to a wetland that contains two equally distinct cover (class) types.

columns.name: split_class_definition
columns.description: Used when a wetland contains two equally distinct cover types (classes) that each encompasses at least 30% areal coverage.  This split class definition is used to describe the second class of either the wetlands dominant life form of the vegetation or the physiography and composition of the substrate.

columns.name: split_subclass
columns.description: Numeric code identifying the split subclass

columns.name: split_subclass_name
columns.description: Name assigned to a wetland that contains two equally distinct life forms or substrates (subclasses).

columns.name: split_subclass_definition
columns.description: Used when a wetland contains two equally distinct life forms or substrates (subclass).  This split subclass definition is used to describe the second subclass of either the wetlands distinct life form or substrate.

columns.name: water_regime
columns.description: Alpha code identifying the water regime

columns.name: water_regime_name
columns.description: Name assigned to add description to wetlands and deepwater habitats to indicate duration of flooding or saturation.

columns.name: water_regime_subgroup
columns.description: Applied to define whether a wetlands hydrologic characteristics are controlled by groundwater, nontidal flooding, freshwater tidal or saltwater tidal factors.

columns.name: water_regime_definition
columns.description: Description of water duration within a wetland habitat.

columns.name: modifier1
columns.description: Alpha code identifying the first modifier

columns.name: modifier1_name
columns.description: Modifier name is assigned to further describe wetlands and deepwater habitats within the classification hierarchy.

columns.name: modifier1_group
columns.description: Modifier assigned to further describe wetlands and deepwater habitats within the classification hierarchy.

columns.name: modifier1_subgroup
columns.description: The type of first modifier applied; which include special modifier, water chemistry or soil.

columns.name: modifier1_definition
columns.description: Modifier assigned to further describe wetlands and deepwater habitats within the classification hierarchy based on water chemistry or ph, wetland or deepwater alteration, or soil type.

columns.name: modifier2
columns.description: Alpha-numeric code identifying the second modifier

columns.name: modifier2_name
columns.description: Modifier name assigned to further describe wetlands and deepwater habitats within the classification hierarchy.

columns.name: modifier2_group
columns.description: Second modifier assigned to further describe wetlands and deepwater habitats within the classification hierarchy.

columns.name: modifier2_subgroup
columns.description: The type of second modifier applied; which include special modifier, water chemistry or soil.

columns.name: modifier2_definition
columns.description: Modifier assigned to further describe wetlands and deepwater habitats within the classification hierarchy based on water chemistry or ph, wetland or deepwater alteration, or soil type.

layers.description: This data set represents the extent, approximate location and type of wetlands and deepwater habitats in the United States and its Territories. These data delineate the areal extent of wetlands and surface waters as defined by Cowardin et al. (1979), which represents a biological definition of wetlands and deepwater habitats. There is no attempt to define the limits of proprietary jurisdiction of any Federal, State, or local government, or to establish the geographical scope of the regulatory programs of government agencies. Some wetland habitats may be under represented or excluded in certain areas because of the limitations of aerial imagery as the primary data source used to detect wetlands. These habitats include seagrasses or submerged aquatic vegetation that are found in the intertidal and subtidal zones of estuaries and near shore coastal waters and also some deepwater reef communities (coral or tuberficid worm reefs). These habitats, because of their depth and water clarity, go undetected by most aerial imagery. By policy, the Service also excludes certain types of

as may be defined by the Food Security Act or that do not coincide with the Cowardin et al. definition. Contact the Service's Regional Wetland Coordinator for additional information on what types of farmed wetlands are included on wetland maps. This dataset should be used in conjunction with the Wetlands_Project_Metadata layer, which contains project boundaries, specific wetlands mapping procedures and information on dates, scales and emulsion of imagery used to map the wetlands within specific project boundaries.

columns.name: huc8
columns.description: Watershed file from which the data were extracted. Added as part of processing by NAR.

layers.description: This data set represents the extent, approximate location and type of riparian habitats in the western United States. These data delineate the areal extent of riparian habitats as defined by A System For Mapping Riparian Areas in the United States (USFWS 2009). Certain riparian habitats may be excluded from the National mapping program because of the limitations of aerial imagery as the primary data source used to detect riparian habitats. This dataset should be used in conjuction with the Riparian Mapping Areas layer, which identifies the extent and location of Riparian mapping projects.

columns.name: attribute
columns.description: Alphanumeric code identifying the riparian classification of the polygon. Join with NWI_Code_Definitions_Table.

columns.name: wetland_type
columns.description: General description of the riparian classification.
